correctness.rationale: If a_i=A_ii and b_i=(A²)_ii, the sampled gain is b_i/a_i with weight a_i/S. Zero a_i means Ae_i=0, so no quotient is needed there. Summing gives q. In an eigenbasis decomposition with W_ij=|U_ij|², take J with weight λ_j/S and randomize it to I via W. Then I has the pivot marginal and G_i is E[λ_J|I=i]. Ordinary and conditional Jensen give both convex-order bounds simultaneously. The identity basis attains the spectral law. The trace-zero matrix A²−qA has an orthonormal zero-diagonal frame: choose a zero-quadratic-form unit vector in the span of two opposite-sign eigendirections, then repeat on the trace-zero compression. This works over the reals and in the Hermitian case. Thus the lower endpoint is also attained for all convex losses, and the diagonal condition is necessary and sufficient. The variance is pointwise continuous on the orbit even at a_i=0 because b_i²/a_i≤λ_max² a_i. The real orbit is the continuous image of SO(n) since multiplying a frame by an eigenvector sign flip does not change the conjugated matrix; the unitary orbit is also connected. Therefore the two attained variance endpoints fill the entire stated interval. The one-dimensional and equal-positive-eigenvalue cases give zero variance; the exact (1,4) planar illustration checks the nondegenerate endpoints.
residual_risks: The argument concerns the trace gain from the first exact pivot, not later adaptive pivots, residual Loewner order, or ordinary tail dominance.
The stored real numerical tests were inspected, not executed. They do not certify universal convex losses, the complex case, or all dimensions; the analytic proof covers them.

The classical f-divergence theorem applies to arbitrary convex losses for a finite classical experiment, not merely operator convex functions; Horn's theorem admits real orthostochastic matrices for any majorized pair of real vectors.

Inserting squared size-biased eigenvalues is a substitution into that broader construction, not a new bound requiring a Cholesky-specific lemma.

evidence: Apply the same stochastic matrix to both spectral probability vectors. By monotonicity, D_f(Wr||Wv)≤D_f(r||v), and Jensen gives its nonnegative lower bound. To attain zero apply Horn to r−v; to attain the upper law take W=I. Substituting the candidate spectral vectors yields the entire envelope for every loss, not only an upper estimate for variance.
Variance then uses f corresponding to the square, the endpoints, and continuity of a finite function along a connected orbit. Exact determinism is simply Wr=Wv, i.e. diag(A²−qA)=0.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Once the known pivot gain is expressed as a likelihood ratio, the preceding two general theorems and this single parameter substitution mechanically give all distributional endpoints. No comparison of expectation-only theorems is being used to infer the envelope.

evidence: Set v_j=λ_j/S and r_j=λ_j²/tr(A²). The input likelihood ratio r_j/v_j is λ_j/q on the positive support. The two output probability vectors after W_ij=|U_ij|² are Wv and Wr, with ratio (Wr)_i/(Wv)_i=G_i/q. Thus for f(x)=φ(qx)−φ(q), the output f-divergence is exactly Eφ(G_A)−φ(q), and the input is Eφ(Λ)−φ(q).

The same W makes all sampled gains equal exactly when W(r−v)=0. The signed vector r−v sums to zero, hence majorizes the zero vector, and Horn gives such an orthostochastic W in every dimension. The identity W gives the other extreme.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is an exact identification of the objective and both orbit endpoints with a general finite binary statistical experiment. Data processing contracts its convex likelihood-ratio dispersion; Schur–Horn produces the zero-information experiment within the real orbit itself. No uniform real flat matrix is assumed. Finite convex losses with endpoint issues are also covered directly by finite Jensen, or by convex interpolation on the finite set of ratios.

The variance interval and determinism criterion are immediate topology and the equality equation, respectively. This is not a claim that the cited RPCholesky algorithm papers literally state the envelope.

value.rationale: The example clarifies that first-step mean invariance does not ensure identical convex risk. But the submitted exact orbit result gives the textbook best and worst experiments for a pair of probability vectors, specialized to a known pivot ratio; all endpoints, the deterministic equation and the variance interval are immediate from the general theorems and continuity. No new one-step invariant beyond those implications, later-step theorem, or construction with a new algorithmic constraint is established.
residual_risks: The exact specialization can still be pedagogical or useful notation for applications. The negative judgment concerns incremental value as an independent result, not the practical RPCholesky analysis or classical implications themselves.
